verses.text: Then Job answered:
“Of course, you’re the only people who know anything. When you die, I guess wisdom dies with you.
But I can think just as well as you can. I’m no less than you. Who doesn’t already know these things?
I’ve become the joke of my neighbors, me, the one who called on God and got an answer. A person can be just and blameless and still be the joke.
People who have it easy look down on trouble. They have contempt ready for anyone whose foot slips.
Robbers’ tents thrive. Those who provoke God live in safety, carrying their god in their own hands.
“But go ask the animals. They’ll teach you. Ask the birds in the sky. They’ll tell you.
Talk to the earth, and it’ll teach you. The fish in the sea will tell you too.
Who among all these doesn’t know that the LORD’s hand has done this?
In his hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of every human being.
Doesn’t the ear test words the way your mouth tastes food?
Wisdom comes with age, and understanding with many years.
“God has wisdom and strength. He knows what to do and understands what’s going on.
Look, when he tears something down, nobody can build it back up. When he locks someone up, nobody can let them out.
When he holds back the waters, they dry up. When he sends them out, they overturn the land.
Strength and wisdom are his. Both the one who gets fooled and the one who fools them are his.
He leads advisers away stripped and turns judges into fools.
He undoes the bonds of kings and ties a belt around their waists.
He leads priests away stripped and brings down the mighty.
He takes the words away from people everyone trusts and strips the elders of their understanding.
He pours contempt on rulers and loosens the belts of the strong.
He brings hidden things up out of darkness and brings the shadow of death into the light.
He makes nations grow, and he destroys them. He makes nations spread, and he leads them away captive.
He takes away the understanding of the earth’s leaders and leaves them wandering in a wilderness with no path.
They feel their way through the dark without a light. He makes them stagger like someone who’s drunk.”
